anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves exactly the three intended facts and regresses none. Cases B and C now put the [recommended] tag on merge at row 1 with recommended=1 in the gate line, Case C's merge consequence names the ruleset bypass while stating that CI evidence stands (no separate bypass action, no claim that CI is bypassed), and every case gains a one-line prose reason immediately above 'Pick one' that ties the recommendation to the case's state (preconditions hold, bypass eligible, WRITE missing). Cases A and D are unchanged in substance, stop stays last, evidence remains hint-only, and no pick or action is simulated. One small tightening to consider: the Case A and B reasons both read 'every merge precondition holds' and are identical; naming the distinguishing state explicitly (e.g. 'you are the author, so approve is not offered' for A, 'merge_state_status CLEAN and reviewDecision APPROVED on robin's PR' for B) would make the 'names the case's state' requirement unambiguous without altering any menu row or the recommendation ordering.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly: Cases B and C now put merge on row 1 with the only [recommended] tag and recommended=1 in the gate line, Case C's merge row carries the bypass consequence without a separate bypass action or any claim that CI is bypassed, Case D keeps approve on row 1 with merge omitted and now states the WRITE-permission reason in prose, and every report has a recommendation sentence immediately above Pick one with stop last and show evidence hint-only. Nothing that Before kept was lost. Two things to tighten: the reason sentence in Cases A and B is identical ("all merge prerequisites hold"), so it names the readiness state but not what distinguishes the case; wording like "Merge is recommended because the viewer can merge and all merge prerequisites hold (own PR; approve not offered)" for A and "...another author's ready PR, so merge outranks approve" for B would make the state-naming unambiguous.
